# A test drives a text input's payload events -- `c.field.input({value=…})`
# and `c.field.change({value=…})` -- and every target runs the handler the
# program wrote, once, with that value, as the interpreter does.
#
# The invokers for these were missing or took the wrong thing:
#
#   - The Go test lowerer passed the payload as a Go `InputEvent{Value: …}`,
#     a type no Go target declares; an invoker takes the widget's value, the
#     payload's `value`, as android's performTextReplacement already does.
#   - bubbletea ran neither handler at all: an input widget synced its bound
#     var and dropped the @input and @change bodies. It now runs @input when
#     an Update changed the text and @change on Enter.
#   - fyne had no @change on an entry (OnSubmitted is its commit), read the
#     payload only in a handler shaped like the two-way bind, and invoked the
#     callback with it attached, so the handler's write-back of the bound
#     text fired it a second time.
#   - gtk4's invokers took no argument, had no commit signal to fire
#     (`activate`), and read the payload only in the bind shape.
#   - html dispatched the DOM event without putting the value in the element
#     the handler reads it from.
#
# Driving `change` runs the change handler alone -- `edits` stays 0 -- where a
# user committing text would have typed it first; the interpreter's reading.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

[gtk4] sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
[gtk4] stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

component editor node {
    var name = ""
    var edits = 0
    var lastCommit = ""

    input #field(
        value=name,
        @input(e) {
            name = e.value
            edits = edits + 1
        },
        @change(e) { lastCommit = e.value + "!" },
    )
    text(value=name)
}

func testInputFiresOnEachKeystroke(t Test, c editor) {
    t.assert(c.name == "")
    c.field.input({value="h"})
    t.assert(c.name == "h")
    c.field.input({value="hello"})
    t.assert(c.name == "hello")
    t.assert(c.edits == 2)
}

func testChangeFiresOnCommit(t Test, c editor) {
    c.field.change({value="committed"})
    t.assert(c.lastCommit == "committed!")
    t.assert(c.edits == 0)
}

window {
}
